Alternatives are properly tested: H2/dep-6111 contradicted by the 8-min quiet gap, zero market-data errors, no direct edge, and no deserialization signature [F13,F16,F17,F7]; H4's GC-thrash branch now indirectly excluded by flat memory [F22,F37], restarts=0 [F25], and absent GC telemetry [F21,F26]; H3 has no change record or telemetry pointing at redis-cache [F20]; cfg-3118 ruled out by timing [F19]. Residuals are acknowledged, not blocking: no revert/intervention test was run, and the config-audit shard-2/3 partial (tc-006) could hide an unseen change — but no such change would plausibly supersede a flag whose activation targets the exact observed slow path inside the degrading service. H5 is untestable but moot (single caller), correctly ranked low. Confidence 0.82 is defensible; I would not go higher because the pure-compute proportionality is still indirect (no per-flag request-count metric) and the intervention positive control is absent.

challenges.issue: The mechanism is demonstrated by co-timing (flag ramp + flat traffic + CPU/latency/error step all in the 12:04-12:05 buckets) rather than by a positive control. No per-flag request-count metric exists to measure the flagged share directly, and no partial rollback of cfg-3120 was observed to show CPU/latency returning to ~40%/~60ms. Proportionality (~2.5x CPU for ~20x flagged share) remains an inference (F38), not a measurement.

Sub-minute onset within the 12:04 bucket is unresolved: the config-applied log is 12:04:16Z and the 12:04 bucket still shows pre-ramp CPU (38.22%)/latency (60.53ms), so the flag-to-effect lag is consistent with but not tightly bounded by the data.

redis-cache (shared by both quote-path hops) was never directly instrumented: get_service_dependencies(redis-cache, downstream) returned an empty edge list [F32], so a redis-side event with no accompanying change record cannot be positively excluded. It is unsupported rather than refuted.

The broader-blast-radius hop is untestable because pricing-engine has a single caller in the graph [F28,F30]. This is not evidence of a shared-component fault, but it is also not evidence against one; the hypothesis stays active only as an artifact of an unobservable dimension.
